topics.title: Concept of Self
topics.ncert_sections: Concept of Self; Self as Subject and Self as Object; Kinds of Self

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish personal identity from social identity using a person's self-descriptions.
Explain the dual status of the self as a subject (knower) and as an object (known).
Describe the biological, personal and social (relational) self and how they emerge.

topics.title: Cognitive and Behavioural Aspects of Self

concepts.learning_objective: Define self-concept and self-esteem and relate self-esteem to behaviour and parenting.
Explain self-efficacy, its basis in Bandura's social learning theory and how it develops.
Apply the techniques of self-regulation and self-control to everyday situations.
Compare the Indian and Western views of the boundary between self and other.
Relate individualistic and collectivistic cultures to the way self and group are related.

topics.title: Concept of Personality
topics.ncert_sections: Concept of Personality; Box 2.1 Personality-related Terms

concepts.learning_objective: State the origin and psychological meaning of the term personality.
Identify the main features of personality and use them to understand and deal with people.
Distinguish temperament, trait, disposition, character, habit and values.

topics.title: Type and Trait Approaches
topics.ncert_sections: Type Approaches; Trait Approaches; Box 2.2 Five-Factor Model

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the typologies of Hippocrates, Charak Samhita, Sheldon, Jung and Friedman and Rosenman.
Explain the trait theories of Allport, Cattell and Eysenck.
Interpret a personality description in terms of the Big Five factors.
Explain Freud's levels of consciousness, structure of personality and stages of development.
Identify ego defence mechanisms such as repression, projection, denial, reaction formation and rationalisation.
Describe the contributions of Jung, Horney, Adler, Fromm and Erikson.

topics.title: Behavioural, Cultural and Humanistic Approaches
topics.ncert_sections: Behavioural Approach; Cultural Approach; Humanistic Approach; Box 2.3

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the behavioural approach views personality as learnt responses to the environment.
Explain personality as an adaptation to the ecological and cultural demands of a group.
Explain Rogers' real and ideal self and Maslow's idea of self-actualisation.

topics.title: Assessment of Personality
topics.ncert_sections: Assessment of Personality; Self-report Measures; Projective Techniques; Behavioural Analysis

concepts.learning_objective: Describe MMPI, EPQ and 16PF and the problems of self-report measures.
Explain the assumptions, features and examples of projective techniques.
Describe interview, observation, ratings, nomination and situational tests and their limitations.
